title: Computational Matter Zoo — Idea Quality & Diversity

source.order: Hydration extraction order; not asserted chronological
source.unavailable: Redacted plugin outputs and linked sandbox notebook artifacts were not recovered.
source.method: Deduplicated user/assistant message IDs from the public shared-page hydration payload; exact source spans retained per idea.

method.unit: Canonical research-idea family; includes evaluable ideas and flagged analogies. Not paper or device ranking.

axes.name: Specification
anchors: Executable contract or fully specified discriminating test

axes.name: Discriminating power
anchors: Counterexample or controlled test isolates the claimed distinction

axes.name: Near-term tractability
anchors: Can test a central premise cheaply now

axes.name: Scientific leverage
anchors: Could revise useful distinctions or connect several validated domains

method.scoreSemantics: Parent-synthesized ordinal formulation judgments, not empirical merit. Each axis has ±1 bounded sensitivity, not statistical uncertainty.
method.queueGate: Specification>=3, discrimination>=3, tractability>=2. This admits bounded experiments, not scientifically validated elites.
method.frontier: Pareto comparison on four formulation axes within the same declared niche and queue eligibility; ties preserved. No weighted total or global winner.
method.diversitySemantics: Primary categorical tags summarize what changes and what is studied. Cross-cutting mechanisms remain visible in full records. Four-by-four grid is a declared display, not a complete universe.
method.dedup: Merge repeated wording and substrate-only variants; split when intervention, response or falsifier differs.
method.novelty: Potential novelty as synthesis, known-method application, stretch or analogy. Literature novelty unknown.
method.reviewProtocol: Three separate first passes; each was instructed not to read peer conclusions. First-pass files frozen with SHA256 before parent synthesis. No salted pre-registration was used for these reviews.
method.runtime: Live review contexts plus Python/NumPy/SciPy controls; no completed Sakana investigation.

ideas.title: Quotient-aware, loop-sensitive QD

source.quote: Removing representational redundancy while preserving loop-sensitive relations

ideas.scoreRationale: Explicit equivalence tests and low-cost counterexamples make this the strongest anchor. The triangle establishes a failure of spectrum-only descriptors, not a new physical discovery.
ideas.claim: Ignore local phase conventions while retaining loop relations that change a declared routing task.
ideas.nextTest: Compare raw, eigenvalue and invariant-response descriptors on new graph families and unseen contacts.
ideas.baseline: Direct scattering descriptors; canonical gauge fixing; identical proposal pool.
ideas.falsifier: No gain in distinct robust responses per total solver and inference cost.
ideas.confounds: Fixed port labels, allowed permutations, time reversal, contacts, energy window and tolerance.

ideas.title: Transfer-operator repertoires

source.quote: diversity of independently addressable input-output transformations

ideas.scoreRationale: The response object is precise and useful across substrates. A repertoire still needs a distance, thresholds and cost budget; resolvent rank alone is not task capacity.
ideas.claim: Search controllable families C(zI-A)^-1 B rather than mode counts.
ideas.nextTest: Fix ports and a noise floor; measure distinguishable responses across held-out controls, frequencies and costs.
ideas.baseline: Spectrum-only search; random controls; conventional programmable network.
ideas.falsifier: Many response differences collapse below readout noise or require impractical control energy.
ideas.confounds: Input normalization, bandwidth, operating state, crosstalk and correlated singular channels.

ideas.title: Counterexample-driven descriptor revision

source.quote: remains nonredundant after conditioning on existing descriptors

ideas.scoreRationale: This supplies a falsifiable meaning of seeing the previously unseen. Formal residual content is relative to a schema and does not by itself establish useful scientific novelty.
ideas.claim: Promote a descriptor only when it predicts consequential distinctions missed by the frozen schema.
ideas.nextTest: Split training and final evaluation; propose descriptors on anomalies and test held-out prediction with complexity penalties.
ideas.baseline: Fixed rich descriptor; random feature additions; manual physicist revision.
ideas.falsifier: New descriptor adds no held-out information or changes only the scoreboard.
ideas.confounds: Adaptive overfitting, post-selection, redundant features, noisy derivatives and schema migration.

ideas.title: Three coupled archives with local schema forks

source.quote: three coupled QD archives

ideas.scoreRationale: A valuable architecture for preserving dissent, though the causal role of each archive needs separate ablations. More maps do not automatically mean more mechanisms.
ideas.claim: Preserve matter, representation and communication-policy alternatives without immediate consensus.
ideas.nextTest: Freeze candidate data; compare one map with competing maps and versioned schema forks on new tasks.
ideas.baseline: One validated response archive; fixed ensembles of representations.
ideas.falsifier: Forks add coordination cost without better prediction or discovery.
ideas.confounds: Common simulator bias, schema proliferation, migration loss and selection feedback.

ideas.title: Anomaly-triggered temporary agent coalitions

source.quote: integration should be anomaly-conditioned, not continuous

ideas.scoreRationale: The trigger and coalition output are concrete. Existing deterministic replays and a small live coalition do not estimate strategy superiority.
ideas.claim: Open bounded communication when normalized representations disagree on the same candidate pair.
ideas.nextTest: Randomize single integrator, broadcast, isolated and event-triggered arms across repeated tasks; match inference, solver calls and tools.
ideas.baseline: Random messaging and fixed sparse graph at the same message budget.
ideas.falsifier: Event routing fails to improve frozen held-out discovery or loses after overhead.
ideas.confounds: Same model errors, token accounting, threshold tuning, shared tools and exploration starvation.

ideas.title: Human similarity feedback with AI scaling

source.quote: Which pair represents more genuinely different physics?

ideas.scoreRationale: A sensible established tool rather than an original invention. The novel opportunity is teaching physical equivalence and useful difference, not maximizing approval.
ideas.claim: Learn mechanism similarity from comparisons, then use calibrated AI judgments between human reviews.
ideas.nextTest: Blind experts to labels; collect disagreement and repeats; evaluate on held-out interventions and unseen mechanisms.
ideas.baseline: Hand-crafted response metric; AI-only judgments; random query selection.
ideas.falsifier: Learned distances track visual language or expert fashion without functional discrimination.
ideas.confounds: Rater expertise, anchoring, inconsistent comparisons, AI-human calibration and prestige cues.

ideas.title: Complementary modal ecology

source.quote: diversity of modes

ideas.scoreRationale: The ambition is broad and physically meaningful. An additive modal-diversity sum is currently underspecified and may double-count frequency, lifetime and localization.
ideas.claim: Co-design extended, localized, rotational and long-lived modes with selective usable couplings.
ideas.nextTest: Use one mechanical model with fixed actuators; test transport and write/read tasks alongside stability.
ideas.baseline: Single-task optimizer and mode-count maximization under equal constraints.
ideas.falsifier: Added modes are inaccessible, unstable or do not enlarge the usable task repertoire.
ideas.confounds: Rigid-body zero modes, degeneracy, incompatible objectives and correlated descriptors.

ideas.title: Small defect or prestress, large functional change

source.quote: prestress changes the modal landscape without changing topology

ideas.scoreRationale: Strong physical precedent makes this tractable. High response per tiny change can be a fragility metric rather than an engineering benefit.
ideas.claim: Find bounded structural or prestress interventions that switch a useful response while retaining stability.
ideas.nextTest: Sweep perturbation size with matched random defects; check response, stability margin and fabrication tolerance.
ideas.baseline: Random bond removal; standard sensitivity optimization.
ideas.falsifier: Gains vanish away from instability or within realistic noise and tolerances.
ideas.confounds: Units of perturbation norm, critical fragility, buckling, damping and eigenvector sign/basis ambiguity.

ideas.title: Rare nonlinear resonance as a gate

source.quote: selection rules are the program

ideas.scoreRationale: Potentially distinctive function with a clear falsifier. Frequency matching alone does not establish a nonzero interaction or an AND gate.
ideas.claim: Couple otherwise separate sectors only for chosen joint inputs, frequencies or amplitudes.
ideas.nextTest: Simulate a specified three-mode nonlinear system; measure truth table, off-target leakage, detuning and noise.
ideas.baseline: Always-coupled linear mixer and equal-energy single inputs.
ideas.falsifier: Output appears for single inputs or disappears under small detuning at useful power.
ideas.confounds: Energy source, symmetry selection rules, nonlinear coefficient magnitudes and unwanted resonances.

ideas.title: Non-normal transient and resolvent diversity

source.quote: Non-normal dynamics

ideas.scoreRationale: A clean counterexample to eigenvalue sufficiency. Our two-state illustration checks the phenomenon; useful computation and hardware realization remain separate.
ideas.claim: Equal eigenvalues can hide different finite-time gains and input-output sensitivity.
ideas.nextTest: Compare stable matrices with identical spectra, then score useful signal/noise task performance under normalized inputs.
ideas.baseline: Normal matrix with same eigenvalues and same allowed energy budget.
ideas.falsifier: Gain amplifies noise or saturates without task benefit.
ideas.confounds: Choice of norm and units, B/C interfaces, physical energy supply and nonlinear saturation.

ideas.title: Programmable moiré carrier routing

source.quote: What moiré landscape makes the electrons naturally implement it?

ideas.scoreRationale: High potential leverage but a weak first hackathon target. The broad device stack lacks a calibrated model and performance comparison.
ideas.claim: Use gates, twist-induced potentials and contacts to select internal-state-dependent routing channels.
ideas.nextTest: First specify one continuum/tight-binding model and realistic contact/disorder distribution; validate selective transmission.
ideas.baseline: Ordinary gate-defined electron optics and photonic routing at matched constraints.
ideas.falsifier: The effect requires inaccessible controls or vanishes with contacts and disorder.
ideas.confounds: Temperature, twist inhomogeneity, interactions, dephasing, contact selectivity and fabrication.

ideas.title: Stateful spin or ferroelectric routing

source.quote: State-dependent routing

ideas.scoreRationale: Statefulness gives a different function from a static scattering matrix. Co-locating memory and routing has costs that the transcript has not quantified.
ideas.claim: Store a persistent state that selects subsequent signal pathways.
ideas.nextTest: Choose one explicit state variable; test write/read retention, switching, fatigue and energy in a calibrated model.
ideas.baseline: Stateless router plus external memory and controller.
ideas.falsifier: Equivalent function is cheaper or more reliable with separated memory and routing.
ideas.confounds: Retention-write tradeoff, hysteresis, read disturbance, thermal drift and control overhead.

ideas.title: Cross-carrier conversion primitives

source.quote: one physical representation can be converted into another

ideas.scoreRationale: Potentially orthogonal to simple routing, but the catalogue is not yet one executable research hypothesis.
ideas.claim: Transfer information among charge, spin, valley, exciton, photon or magnon channels with a useful interface.
ideas.nextTest: Select exactly two carriers and a measurable transducer; measure conversion efficiency, noise and bandwidth.
ideas.baseline: Established separate transducer chain.
ideas.falsifier: Conversion losses and added controls dominate any computational benefit.
ideas.confounds: Incompatible scales, baths, impedance, reciprocity, quantum/classical distinctions and readout.

ideas.title: Intervention-first ALife mechanism mining

source.quote: The object worth archiving is therefore not just an organism or a matrix

ideas.scoreRationale: One of the strongest long-term directions. Its novelty lies in the intervention-based synthesis and transfer test, not the existence of automated ALife search.
ideas.claim: Mine reproducible memory, recovery and conditional response mechanisms rather than appearance alone.
ideas.nextTest: Search one simulator using visual novelty versus held-out intervention signatures, matching evaluation cost.
ideas.baseline: ASAL-style visual descriptors; random rules; direct task optimizer.
ideas.falsifier: Response descriptors fail to yield stable distinct mechanisms beyond appearance baselines.
ideas.confounds: Seed, boundary, update convention, visualization bias and external control supplied by simulator.

ideas.title: Writable/readable memory and basin geometry

source.quote: A slowly changing internal variable is not automatically useful memory

ideas.scoreRationale: High information per experiment. Equal local Jacobians need not imply equal global basins; our illustration confirms only that premise, not a memory device.
ideas.claim: Separate persistent activity from a state that inputs can write, outputs can read, and perturbations do not erase.
ideas.nextTest: Use separate write, delay, distractor, read and reset phases; test held-out histories and noise.
ideas.baseline: Linear fading memory and bistable state with identical local derivative where feasible.
ideas.falsifier: Persistent state cannot be written/read reliably or carries no information about inputs.
ideas.confounds: Readout capacity, hidden forcing, basin sampling, saturation and selective reporting.

ideas.title: Time-windowed channels and Floquet response

source.quote: channels that are mostly closed

ideas.scoreRationale: This can reveal a genuine blind spot of stationary spectra. Floquet methods require periodic behavior; general trajectories require time-varying kernels.
ideas.claim: Detect channels open at specific phases or times along moving or periodic patterns.
ideas.nextTest: Measure phase-conditioned perturbation kernels and predict new timing-dependent responses.
ideas.baseline: Stationary average transfer function; randomized intervention times.
ideas.falsifier: Time-conditioned model fails out of sample or adds no discrimination beyond state.
ideas.confounds: Phase registration, nonstationarity, trajectory alignment, finite-amplitude perturbations and state leakage.

ideas.title: Verified Koopman features for ALife

source.quote: This feature survives changes in data, resolution, observable dictionary

ideas.scoreRationale: Useful representation candidate with explicit verification. Linear operator notation does not guarantee a finite exact reduction of nonlinear dynamics.
ideas.claim: Accept spectral observables only when residual and held-out response tests support them.
ideas.nextTest: Vary dictionaries, resolution, horizons and seeds; compare intervention prediction and residuals.
ideas.baseline: Linearization, delay embedding and direct finite-time response estimator.
ideas.falsifier: Modes disappear with dictionaries or fail response predictions.
ideas.confounds: Spectral pollution, hidden state, finite samples, continuous spectrum and uncontrolled inputs.

ideas.title: Boundary-programmable transformation repertoires

source.quote: The surrounding material becomes part of the program

ideas.scoreRationale: A particularly clean ALife starting point. Our exhaustive 256-rule toy protocol is new here and is not a reproduction of the source notebook or the full published study.
ideas.claim: Count which input-output functions a region can perform under different surrounding initial states.
ideas.nextTest: Enumerate small rules with explicit boundary/time/input protocol; separately score bijectivity, information and noise.
ideas.baseline: Random rules; high transformation count without input preservation.
ideas.falsifier: Large repertoires consist mostly of constant or indistinguishable functions.
ideas.confounds: Region size, evolving versus clamped environment, time horizon and input prior.

ideas.title: Coherent structures and interaction grammars

source.quote: local causal-state work discovers domains, coherent structures, and interactions

ideas.scoreRationale: A different route from spectra to computational primitives. Particle-like patterns are not literal quantum quasiparticles.
ideas.claim: Find predictively distinct traveling structures and test their collision logic as reusable operations.
ideas.nextTest: Identify structures on training trajectories; intervene on timing and context and test a held-out interaction table.
ideas.baseline: Shape tracking; raw-state predictors; chance encounter statistics.
ideas.falsifier: Particle labels do not predict interaction outcomes beyond raw states.
ideas.confounds: Coarse graining, temporal windows, observer-dependent labels and untested contexts.

ideas.title: Adaptive ecologies and history-gated coupling

source.quote: The thing to mine is not just the oscillators

ideas.scoreRationale: Broader than a static modal zoo and worth preserving as a separate niche. The proposed slow-variable model is currently schematic.
ideas.claim: Search coexisting organizations whose slow state controls when they exchange influence.
ideas.nextTest: Use causal perturbations of the proposed slow variable; measure conditional coupling and preserved independent function.
ideas.baseline: Fixed coupling with matched mean interaction strength; common-input controls.
ideas.falsifier: Apparent gating is explained by common forcing, density or measurement phase.
ideas.confounds: Ecological context, mass conservation, latent state, nonlocal rules and external energy.

ideas.title: Compile ALife into minimal physical mechanisms

source.quote: The transfer criterion should be agreement on interventions

ideas.scoreRationale: High potential novelty as an integrated experiment. A matching animation or eigenvalue spectrum is not mechanism transfer or hardware advantage.
ideas.claim: Reduce an ALife behavior to a minimal dynamical model, then realize its tested intervention responses in another substrate.
ideas.nextTest: Fit on one intervention family; test new histories, damage and noise in source and reduced target with an explicit resource ledger.
ideas.baseline: Black-box emulator; standard reservoir; simple recurrent dynamical system.
ideas.falsifier: Transfer succeeds only on training traces or requires unavailable nonlocal controls.
ideas.confounds: Identifiability, reduction fidelity, control/readout energy, bandwidth and substrate calibration.

ideas.title: Topology beyond ordinary localization

source.quote: distinguishes real topology from ordinary localization

ideas.scoreRationale: A necessary skeptical track. Localization or a visually striking edge mode alone does not establish topology.
ideas.claim: Preserve robust boundary or defect behaviors only when the claimed invariant and perturbation class justify protection.
ideas.nextTest: Compare topological and nontopological localized controls under symmetry-preserving and symmetry-breaking disorder.
ideas.baseline: Ordinary defect mode with matched frequency/localization.
ideas.falsifier: Robustness is reproduced without topology or disappears within the claimed protected class.
ideas.confounds: Boundary conditions, finite size, gap closing, symmetry, non-Hermitian conventions and actuator coupling.

ideas.title: Higher-order coalitions and structured TTC

source.quote: a three-way reasoning interaction need not equal three pairwise interactions

ideas.scoreRationale: The hypothesis is testable once hyperedge semantics are explicit. Drawing a filled triangle does not create an irreducible multiway interaction.
ideas.claim: Test whether a joint context enables functions unavailable to matched pairwise exchanges.
ideas.nextTest: Construct tasks with known multiway dependencies; compare hyperedge and pairwise protocols under matched tokens, rounds and tools.
ideas.baseline: Pairwise relay with equal total information; single integrator.
ideas.falsifier: Equal information pairwise communication matches performance and cost.
ideas.confounds: Hidden broadcast, context length, nonlinear aggregator and incomparable communication budgets.

ideas.title: Sheaf compatibility and Hodge disagreement

source.quote: Can these local beliefs be consistently reconciled?

ideas.scoreRationale: Useful formal machinery when the mathematical objects exist. A preference cycle alone is not automatically a cohomological obstruction; H1 nonzero does not mean no global section.
ideas.claim: Encode explicit translations or restrictions and distinguish inconsistency from representational mismatch.
ideas.nextTest: Start with finite symbolic constraints with known satisfying assignments; test localization and compare plain constraint solving.
ideas.baseline: SAT/constraint graph; weighted residual checks; majority voting.
ideas.falsifier: Topological score gives no useful diagnosis beyond simpler constraints or depends on arbitrary embedding.
ideas.confounds: Choice of stalks/maps/filled faces, inequality versus vector constraints and semantic embedding validity.

ideas.title: OT or curvature-driven communication routing

source.quote: routing itself becomes

ideas.scoreRationale: Interesting policy variants, but OT distance is not automatically semantic work and curvature does not directly measure information value. Keep separate diagnostics in implementation.
ideas.claim: Allocate communication using a calibrated hypothesis-space transport cost or graph bottleneck diagnostic.
ideas.nextTest: Define the cost/graph precisely; randomize equal-budget communication and measure held-out task benefit.
ideas.baseline: Shortest path, uncertainty-triggered and random sparse routing.
ideas.falsifier: Curvature or transport adds computation without improving scientific yield.
ideas.confounds: Arbitrary semantic ground metric, sign conventions, degree effects and positive curvature as false redundancy proxy.

ideas.title: Macro-level goal control and error correction

source.quote: communication is not automatically collective intelligence

ideas.scoreRationale: A worthwhile functional test. The proposed ratio of goal-space sizes is undefined without measures and does not establish a new cognitive individual.
ideas.claim: Ask whether a collective can retain a macro-level goal under perturbations through adaptive division of labor.
ideas.nextTest: Specify macro-variable and success region; disable recruitment/control and perturb subagents under matched resources.
ideas.baseline: Fixed team and centralized controller.
ideas.falsifier: Performance is fully explained by extra resources or one controlling component.
ideas.confounds: Anthropomorphism, goal attribution, hidden human correction and incomparable goal spaces.

ideas.title: A calibrated fidelity and resource ladder

source.quote: promising results must climb a

ideas.scoreRationale: Essential to the project, though availability depends on calibration and tools. NumPy calculation alone cannot supply material-specific parameters or phase diagrams.
ideas.evidence: Plan; no DFT or device run
ideas.claim: Move candidates from cheap models to calibrated simulation and experiment while preserving uncertainty and costs.
ideas.nextTest: Preselect random and elite candidates for higher-fidelity validation; estimate ranking transfer and failure modes.
ideas.baseline: Cheap-model-only selection; random validation; standard multifidelity optimizer.
ideas.falsifier: Toy elites fail systematically at higher fidelity or total validation cost erases search gains.
ideas.confounds: Selection bias, uncertain force constants/hoppings, model discrepancy, solver error and failed validations.

ideas.title: Universality through reverse diversity search

source.quote: which discovers **universality**

ideas.scoreRationale: An overlooked counterweight to novelty search. Failure under richer tests is informative; finite behavioral agreement must not be called universal physical equivalence.
ideas.claim: Search structurally distant systems with indistinguishable tested responses, alongside nearby systems with large response changes.
ideas.nextTest: Fit response-matched pairs on training inputs; distinguish them with new ports, frequencies and histories.
ideas.baseline: Random structurally distant pairs and standard model reduction.
ideas.falsifier: Equivalence breaks immediately under modest new interventions or is caused by a blind interface.
ideas.confounds: Task-scoped equivalence versus exact conjugacy, coarse response tolerance and inaccessible state.

ideas.title: Evolve selection policies as well as candidates

source.quote: evolving how search selects candidates

ideas.scoreRationale: Distinct from changing descriptors or agent messaging. This remains an underdeveloped lead rather than a worked algorithm in the source.
ideas.claim: Adapt the balance between diversification and fitness using a policy that transfers across task families.
ideas.nextTest: Train selection on some worlds and test unseen worlds with equal evaluation budgets.
ideas.baseline: Fixed MAP-Elites, novelty search, random and hand-tuned mixtures.
ideas.falsifier: Meta-policy fails transfer or consumes its apparent gain in training cost.
ideas.confounds: Meta-overfitting, benchmark leakage, reward definition and amortization horizon.

ideas.title: Physics-inspired reasoning phase taxonomy

source.quote: tensegrity-style phase transitions in reasoning

ideas.scoreRationale: Useful ideation pressure but currently the weakest scientific formulation. Ferromagnetic, Weyl, exciton and tensor labels do not yet define separate validated computational mechanisms.
ideas.claim: Use physical analogies to propose measurable coordination regimes rather than infer them from terminology.
ideas.nextTest: Choose one analogy, define state/update/control/order parameter, then test a predicted transition against null processes.
ideas.baseline: Ordinary modular graph or state machine with the same resources.
ideas.falsifier: No distinct prediction survives replacing the physics vocabulary with a generic model.
ideas.confounds: Category errors, entropy without specified measure, tensor rank versus diversity and unsupported phase-transition language.

ideas.title: Gauge-invariant relational correction to attention

source.quote: small relational correction channel

ideas.scoreRationale: The factorization Uij=gamma_i conjugate(gamma_j) forces every loop product to one. This identifies an algebraic missing capability, not a proven neural architecture gain.
ideas.claim: Add a bounded loop-feature channel that carries relations not expressible as node-phase differences.
ideas.nextTest: Compare pure-gauge factorized links with independent loop links on known cycle-dependent tasks at matched parameters and compute.
ideas.baseline: Softmax attention, efficient attention and extra nonrelational features with equal capacity.
ideas.falsifier: Loop channel adds no held-out task benefit or destroys intended scaling.
ideas.confounds: Cycle enumeration, phase wrapping, feature leakage, orientation conventions and complexity versus input-output linearity.

ideas.title: Audit observational aliasing beyond exact symmetries

source.quote: an insufficient measurement protocol still merges distinct states

ideas.scoreRationale: This is a separate and easily overlooked idea: removing coordinate copies and discovering blind measurements solve opposite errors. Our two-state restricted-interface example verifies only a concrete alias.
ideas.claim: Treat finite response equality as a provisional statement and actively search for a discriminating intervention.
ideas.nextTest: Find models matching training measurements; open a new port, energy or input history and measure whether the equivalence breaks.
ideas.baseline: Fixed narrow protocol; random additional measurements; exact known-symmetry controls.
ideas.falsifier: Adaptive measurement adds no discrimination per cost or falsely separates known equivalents.
ideas.confounds: Noise threshold, hidden states, selected operating conditions and inaccessible interventions.

ideas.title: Adaptive routing with low-exposure exploration probes

source.quote: cross-modal probes

ideas.scoreRationale: Distinct from deciding when one coalition opens. Updating scientific synapses needs measured gains and exploration; a disagreement-per-cost score is not calibrated Bayesian information gain.
ideas.claim: Adapt communication strengths from validated scientific yield while probing specialists that current distances would ignore.
ideas.nextTest: Compare fixed, adaptive and adaptive-with-probes policies on new task families, charge all routing and evaluation costs.
ideas.baseline: Random low-exposure probes and fixed sparse communication with equal budget.
ideas.falsifier: Updates overfit the training tasks or probes outperform the learned score alone.
ideas.confounds: Delayed credit, proxy value-of-information, shared feedback loops and selection bias.

limitations: This is an evaluated map of a finite conversation, not a generated discovery campaign or a comprehensive literature review.

Thirty-three canonical families are a human/AI analytical granularity choice. Aliases, substrate variants and repeated assistant answers are merged; useful submechanisms may be split in future versions.

Three complementary reviewers used separate first-pass contexts but share the parent model family and source data. Role specialization does not establish statistical independence. No human ratings were collected.

Four 0–4 formulation axes are distinct questions, not proven statistically orthogonal factors. They are ordinal judgments with ±1 sensitivity bands, not confidence intervals, calibrated probabilities or measured scientific quality.
Novelty potential concerns the proposed synthesis. Literature novelty remains null for every idea; primary-source checks establish selected precedents, not absence of prior art.

The source reports a 7,400-word notebook, five demos and 39 checks. Its sandbox files were not recovered here; those reported numbers are not counted as verified. New local controls use their own explicit protocols.
The Sakana AI Scientist installation did not complete an AI investigation in the preceding run. It did not produce these evaluations.
No physical device, material-specific DFT/thermodynamic calculation, new hardware advantage, or matched-budget multiagent superiority was demonstrated.
Diversity cell occupancy is conditional on this declared schema and corpus. Empty cells are prompts for inquiry, not proof of undiscovered science.
Review files preserve first-pass suggestions. Parent synthesis corrects overclaims and reconciles taxonomic choices; reviewer descriptions are not empirical outcomes.

shortlist.reason: Best executable anchor: test both false novelty and false merging.
Most useful scientific extension: make new descriptors earn predictive value.
Best low-cost ALife entry: finite exhaustive transformation maps with explicit protocol.
Best overlooked control: input-writable and output-readable memory, not persistent activity.
Best coordination hypothesis: repeated randomized matched-budget tests remain necessary.
High-upside stretch: one minimal mechanism transferred under held-out interventions.

corrections.correction: False for fixed interfaces; triangle and non-normal examples supply counterexamples.

corrections.claim: Same finite measured response means gauge equivalence
corrections.correction: Only observational equivalence under that protocol; unobserved states or new interventions can differ.
Fails a six-identical-agent negative control; graph connectivity spectra and representation diversity are separate.

corrections.claim: Any new schema residual is new useful science
corrections.correction: Residual is schema-relative; require added predictive discrimination, robustness and complexity accounting.
Eigenvalues alone do not recover eigenvectors. Retain the operator, state/interface and eigenspaces, especially at degeneracy.

corrections.claim: Graph cycles automatically imply nonlinear reasoning or cohomological obstruction
corrections.correction: Specify state spaces, maps, faces and semantics. Hodge decomposition is linear; a sheaf may have nonzero H1 and still global sections.
Different methods and inputs improve complementarity; shared model, data and solver errors remain.
